title: Trumpet lessons with P.M. Williams
summary: Joe got him a trumpet; P.M. Williams, a circus and carnival player, taught him, but Roy learned by ear and was not really reading, including a church duet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So he talked my people into getting me a horn for Christmas. They got me a trumpet. And I started taking lessons off P.M. Williams.
How do you spell that first name?

Just P.M. Like night, nighttime. But he had played on circuses and carnivals and things like that, and he had some helluva chops, man -- Jesus. If I had listened to him, I would have been really a powerful trumpet player, a legitimate trumpet player, because he... You know, they had them marches. You could hear this cat twenty blocks away, above everybody, you know. He had them good chops,

you know. But my only fault was that I listened to him, but he made the mistake of playing the lesson before I played it. And when he would do that, if I heard it I could play it, you know. And he thought I was reading it. I wasn't reading that.
You picked everything up by ear.

Yeah! Once he played it, I had it, you know. And I'll never forget the first time we played out. We played in church. And he was worried to death because we had a duet to play. And I was talkin' to some of my buddies. He said, "Sit up there and look at your music," you know. It didn't make any difference, I didn't know what it was anyhow, you know. But when the thing came, it went off like clockwork.
